content.value_statement: Obsidian notes can break when math syntax is inconsistent. This skill supplies clear MathJax patterns for equations, matrices, calculus, symbols, and notation.
actual_capabilities: Explains inline and block math delimiters for Obsidian notes.
Provides LaTeX patterns for fractions, roots, powers, and subscripts.
Shows matrix, determinant, aligned equation, and cases examples.
Lists common Greek letters, symbols, operators, and font commands.
References a longer symbol table for MathJax commands.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not render or preview equations itself.
It focuses on Obsidian MathJax behavior, not every LaTeX package.
It does not validate formulas against a live Obsidian vault.
Advanced macros may require separate MathJax configuration.

use_cases.title: Write Study Notes
use_cases.description: Create readable lecture notes with inline formulas, block equations, and common symbol references.

use_cases.title: Draft Research Math
use_cases.description: Format proofs, derivations, matrices, and calculus notation inside an Obsidian research vault.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Standardize mathematical notation for guides, tutorials, and reference pages that use Obsidian.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Simple Equation
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this equation into Obsidian MathJax with inline and block options: [equation].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Matrix Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian note section that explains this matrix operation using MathJax: [operation].

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite Multi-Line Derivation
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this derivation with aligned MathJax, clear line breaks, and short explanations: [derivation].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Complete Math Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a compact Obsidian reference for this topic with symbols, cases, limits, matrices, and notation guidance: [topic].

output_examples.input: A student asks for the chain rule in an Obsidian note.
output_examples.output: A display equation, a brief explanation, and notation guidance for readable calculus notes.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a matrix determinant example.
output_examples.output: A formatted determinant example with delimiter guidance and a short note about row and column placement.

output_examples.input: A writer asks to clean a conditional probability formula.
output_examples.output: A block equation using conditional probability notation, with spacing notes for readable MathJax.

best_practices: Use block math for multi-line equations and derivations.
Use braces around multi-character subscripts and exponents.
Check complex formulas in Obsidian preview before sharing notes.
anti_patterns: Do not mix inline and block delimiters in one formula.
Do not assume every LaTeX package command works in MathJax.
Do not paste large derivations without alignment and line breaks.

faq.question: Does this skill run scripts?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with MathJax examples and symbol tables.

faq.question: Is this only for Obsidian?
faq.answer: It targets Obsidian because Obsidian uses MathJax for note rendering.

faq.question: Can it help with matrices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes matrix environments, determinants, ellipsis patterns, and aligned examples.

faq.question: Can it create calculus notation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers integrals, sums, limits, derivatives, and spacing guidance.

faq.question: Does it include a full symbol list?
faq.answer: It includes common symbols and links to a longer reference file.

faq.question: Will every LaTeX command work?
faq.answer: No. MathJax supports many commands, but some LaTeX packages are unavailable.
